title: Event-driven arrival replay for continuous-batch & queue-feedback benchmarking
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an event-driven arrival replay harness that can reproduce production-like mixed workloads to quantify how continuous batching and queueing/backpressure interact across token-length distributions. The harness should target token/sec throughput surfaces and p95 latency contours and enable automated regression detection against historical baselines.

Why this is different: existing bench harnesses focus on synthetic arrival curves or microburst stress tests. This ticket is to implement a replay-centric driver that injects real arrival timestamps, interleaves multiple customer mixes, and models queue-feedback (adaptive client pacing + server-side pushback) so we can observe emergent batching behavior under realistic backpressure conditions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness reproduces at least three real arrival traces from prod anonymized datasets (short chat, long-completion, embedding-heavy).
2) Exposes configurable queue-feedback models (rate-limiter, token-throttle, early-reject) and supports toggling server-side backpressure responses.
3) Captures per-request tokens, start/finish timestamps, inferred batch sizes, and p95 for end-to-end latency.
4) Produces regression reports (tokens/sec delta, p95 delta, batch-size distribution shift) and can alert when metrics cross configurable thresholds.
5) End-to-end tests and a reference run with fixed seed reproduce previously recorded baseline within 5% for tokens/sec and 10% for p95 on our CI hardware profile.
approach:
- Implement arrival-replay core: parser for anonymized arrival traces and a driver that schedules synthetic client task creation at recorded timestamps.
- Client-side pacing models: constant, adaptive (PID-like), and bursty. These drive request send timing and adapt to observed server pushback.
- Server-side backpressure knobs: token-based throttle, accept-queue-limit, and 429/503 early-reject.
- Instrumentation layer: record per-request metadata (trace_id, payload_tokens, batch_id, enqueue_time, dequeue_time, kernel-exec-time).
- Analysis pipeline: post-run extractor that computes tokens/sec heatmaps by time window, p50/p95/p99 latency curves, batch-size CDFs, and detects regressions vs baseline using A/B-stats with bootstrap confidence intervals.
workloads:
1) Short-chat mix: 70% 16-48 token requests, 30% 128-512 token followups.
2) Long-completion mix: 60% 512-2048 tokens, 40% 128-512 tokens.
3) Embedding/QA hybrid: 50% 1-3 token embedding-style calls (high QPS), 50% 64-256 token QA.
All mixes should support per-tenant weight scaling to create multi-tenant interference scenarios.
metrics_to_collect:
- tokens_per_second (global and per-tenant)
- end_to_end_latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99)
- queue_wait_ms distribution
- observed_batch_size distribution over time windows
- kernel_exec_ms and gpu_utilization
- early_reject_rate and 429/503 counts
- regression_score (composite metric used by alerts)
harness_components:
- arrival-replay CLI (go) that accepts trace files and workload definitions.
- load-generator clients that can simulate adaptive pacing and maintain per-connection KV for session continuity.
- server-side testhooks integrated into runtime to emit enqueue/dequeue events and optional forced backpressure responses.
- analysis library (python) for metrics ingestion, baseline comparison, and PDF/HTML report generation.
- CI job template and a sample baseline artifact stored in artifacts/runtime-bench/baselines/.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Fidelity vs determinism: replaying production traces improves realism but produces higher variance; we mitigate with seedable randomness and repeated runs.
- Complexity: adding server-side testhooks risks coupling benchmark code to runtime; keep testhooks behind feature flags and gated by test-only builds.
- Measurement noise from infra variability: standardize on dedicated CI nodes for baseline runs; capture node-level metrics to normalize results.
- Cost: long long-tail runs (hours) for stable p95 estimates are expensive; provide sampling-mode and high-confidence-mode to trade cost vs statistical power.
